items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: You played with him... I was doing a big band show... And I looked to my left and there was Darius Brubeck playing trombone.

ctx.x: Darius Brubeck? You played with him and everywhere from there to the Coasters.

Yes. Like I say I am versatile and jazz is my music but I bring something from all these experiences into my playing. I was doing a big band show with what I’ll call a vintage big band, it was playing a concert. And I looked to my left and there was Darius Brubeck playing trombone. And an excellent musician. And again he was coming out of his jazz context into the vintage music style to add something to his jazz repertoire. And an excellent musician, and I envy people that can jump from trombone and play bass as…
people automatically expect you to be great. And it’s something you have to deal with when your spouse is a musician.

items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: Danny, yeah, excellent. They’re all fine musicians and something that I found out — that when Paul Desmond passed away he left his saxophone to the Brubeck son who did not choose to play music

ctx.x: His other son is quite a good drummer.

Danny, yeah, excellent. They’re all fine musicians and something that I found out — that when Paul Desmond passed away he left his saxophone to the Brubeck son who did not choose to play music, in hopes that someday he would pick up the saxophone, which I thought was very interesting.
Now let’s see you’ve mentioned Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa and Joe Morello. Who is the player that you like to listen to who you would consider, oh let’s say the most modern?
